evidence.positive: Against the running app (mayo-mayo, shipped antibiotic-pathways.csv: p-pancreatectomy row 0 risk=low CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE, row 1 risk=high CEFTRIAXONE AND METRONIDAZOLE) I built three pancreatectomy cases and read them back through GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates. High-risk case 43997 (risk calculated attribute {"risk":"high"}): 'recommended: [{step 1, drugs [CEFTRIAXONE, METRONIDAZOLE]}]', 'pos=1 risk=HIGH appliesToCase=true', 'pos=0 risk=LOW appliesToCase=false'. Low-risk case 40633 ({"risk":"low"}): 'recommended: [{step 1, drugs [CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE]}]', 'pos=0 risk=LOW appliesToCase=true'. Unrated case 60620 (calculated_attributes = {}): 'ratedRisk=null' yet 'pos=0 risk=LOW appliesToCase=true' and CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE recommended, i.e. an absent risk read as LOW. On the clinician-facing path POST /api/cds/medication-selection, selecting m-cefazolin on the high-risk case raised a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic titled 'CefTRIAXone and MetroNIDAZOLE are recommended' with ALTERNATIVE_ANTIBIOTIC_CANDIDATES = [CEFTRIAXONE+METRONIDAZOLE], and selecting m-ceftriaxone on the low-risk case raised the same rule titled 'CeFAZolin and MetroNIDAZOLE are recommended' with alternatives [CEFAZOLIN+METRONIDAZOLE]. I also uploaded a config adding a third unscoped row 'p-pancreatectomy,,,VANCOMYCIN' via POST /api/admin/config-imports/antibiotic-pathways/upload (200, count 463 -> 464): 'pos=2 risk=null appliesToCase=true' on BOTH the low- and high-risk cases, which is the 'a pathway naming no risk applies at every risk' bullet.
evidence.negative: The pathway written for the other risk level neither survived nor died. On low-risk case 40633 the HIGH row reported 'pos=1 risk=HIGH appliesToCase=false statuses=[[NOT_SELECTED],[NOT_SELECTED]]' - NOT_SELECTED, not CONTRAINDICATED, so it was filtered out before the walk rather than ruled out inside it - and CEFTRIAXONE never appeared in 'recommended'. Symmetrically on high-risk case 43997 the LOW row reported 'pos=0 risk=LOW appliesToCase=false statuses=[[NOT_SELECTED],[NOT_SELECTED]]' and CEFAZOLIN never appeared in 'recommended'. Selecting m-cefazolin on the low-risk case and m-ceftriaxone on the high-risk case both returned no a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic result at all ('ABSENT from results'), so each risk's own drug is accepted silently while the other risk's drug is challenged.
evidence.red_check: Two flips, both reverted. (1) Re-uploaded the Mayo CSV with the Risk column blanked on the two p-pancreatectomy rows (upload 200, 463 -> 463). Low-risk case 40633 then reported 'pos=0 risk=null appliesToCase=true' AND 'pos=1 risk=null appliesToCase=true' with 'recommended: [{CEFAZOLIN,METRONIDAZOLE},{CEFTRIAXONE,METRONIDAZOLE}]' - the high-risk protocol leaked onto a low-risk case - and a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic went ABSENT when m-ceftriaxone was selected on that case. That is the absence assertion going red, and it is exactly the pre-fix 'two protocols competing as tiers of one ladder' behaviour. (2) Re-uploaded with both rows scoped 'high' (upload 200, 463 -> 461): the importer's incomplete-risk-scope guard fired at WARN - 'Dropping the risk-scoped pathways for p-pancreatectomy: only [HIGH] configured, so any other risk would resolve to no guidance at all' - the two rows were removed from antibiotic_pathways (0 rows for p-pancreatectomy) and low-risk case 40633 resolved 'outcome: NOT_CONFIGURED recommended: []'. Both flips reverted by re-uploading the shipped CSV; I diffed the restored upload byte-for-byte against /app/resources/data/org/mayo/procedures/antibiotic-pathways.csv in the container (identical), confirmed antibiotic_pathways is back to position 0 = LOW and position 1 = HIGH, and re-ran the positive and negative cases, which returned to CEFAZOLIN-only on low risk with pos=1 appliesToCase=false and CEFTRIAXONE-only on high risk with pos=0 appliesToCase=false, plus the wrong-antibiotic alert firing again for m-ceftriaxone on low risk.

red_check_signature: Dropping the risk-scoped pathways for p-pancreatectomy: only [HIGH] configured, so any other risk would resolve to no guidance at all
caveats: Procedure risk was written straight into the operation_procedure_types.risk calculated attribute (the same key and token form ProcedureRiskService writes) rather than produced by a live rating, so the rating half of the chain was not re-exercised here.

ProcedureRiskService only rates p-pancreatectomy and only Mayo configures it, and Mayo's POST /api/app-launch needs Epic FHIR OAuth that this instance cannot reach, so a genuinely rated risk was unreachable in this environment.
Only the Mayo config ships risk-scoped rows; demo and MGB antibiotic-pathways.csv have none, so those tenants were unaffected and untested.
The debugger payload was read over the admin API rather than through the rendered In-App Debugger tab; the ticket delivers no UI change of its own.

automation.assessment: Service- and importer-level coverage is already thorough and I would not duplicate it: AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest covers riskScopedPathwayAppliesOnlyAtThatRisk, unscopedPathwayAppliesAtEveryRisk, caseWithoutRiskReadsAsLowRisk, acuityAndRiskAreBothRequired, cache_aRiskChangeDropsEveryReadersAnswerForTheCase and theExplanationListsPathwaysScopedToTheOtherRisk, and AntibioticPathwayCSVImporterTest covers readsTheRiskColumn, readsRiskInEitherTokenForm, blankRiskAppliesToEveryCase, dropsRiskScopedPathwaysUnlessEveryRiskHasOne and keepsRiskScopedPathwaysWhenEveryRiskHasOne. The real gap is the shipped config: MayoProcedureConfigImportIntegrationTest only asserts a total pathway count over 400 and spot-checks p-appendectomy, so if either p-pancreatectomy row were edited or deleted the incomplete-risk-scope guard would silently drop both and that assertion would still pass, leaving the procedure unconfigured with no test failing. There is also no end-to-end coverage of a risk-scoped recommendation reaching a clinician.
proposed_tests: Extend MayoProcedureConfigImportIntegrationTest to pin the shipped p-pancreatectomy pair: exactly two pathways, risks {LOW, HIGH}, notations 'CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE -> LEVOFLOXACIN AND METRONIDAZOLE' and 'CEFTRIAXONE AND METRONIDAZOLE -> LEVOFLOXACIN AND METRONIDAZOLE'.

Add an importer assertion that no shipped org file leaves a procedure with a partially covered risk scope, so a future config edit that trips dropIncompleteRiskScopes fails the build instead of silently unconfiguring the procedure.

Add a supplemental qa-suite clinical-rules case: low-risk pancreatectomy plus ceftriaxone raises a-known-procedure-wrong-antibiotic recommending cefazolin, and the same selection on a high-risk pancreatectomy raises nothing.
Add the inverse supplemental qa-suite case: cefazolin on a high-risk pancreatectomy raises the wrong-antibiotic alert recommending ceftriaxone.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: On the running build a high-risk pancreatectomy resolved to ceftriaxone plus metronidazole while a low-risk one resolved to cefazolin plus metronidazole, and a case with no rating read as low risk.
Negative: The pathway written for the other risk level reported as not applying and its options as not selected rather than contraindicated, so its drugs never reached the recommendation and the wrong-antibiotic alert stayed silent for each risk's own drug.
Red check: Blanking the Risk column on the two pancreatectomy rows and re-importing put ceftriaxone back onto a low-risk case, and scoping both rows to high made the importer drop them and left the procedure unconfigured; both flips were reverted and the correct behaviour re-confirmed.

Automation: Service and importer coverage is already thorough, so the proposal is to pin the shipped Mayo pancreatectomy pair in the config import test and add supplemental end-to-end coverage of the per-risk wrong-antibiotic alert.
